title: Market for oranges
questionText: Consider the market for oranges. What disequilibrium condition would occur if the price of oranges were $3.5kg?
answers: A surplus of 20kg
A surplus of 10kg
A shortage of 10kg
A shortage of 20kg

title: Market for rental houses
questionText: Consider the market for rental housing. At a rental price of $200 per week, which of the following statements is true?
answers: There is a shortage of rental houses. The market is only willing to supply 10,000 houses at this rent level
There is shortage of rental houses. The market is willing to supply 30,000 houses at this rent level
There is a surplus of rental houses. The market is willing to supply 10,000 houses at this rent level
There is a surplus of rental houses. The market is willing to supply 30,000 houses at this rent level

title: Market for rental houses
questionText: At a rental price of $200 per week, what will likely begin the process of the price mechanism operating to restore equilibrium?
answers: Competition for limited housing will cause tenants to bid up the price of rent causing an expansion in supply
Competition for limited housing will cause tenants to bid up the price of rent causing a contraction in demand
Competition for limited housing will cause tenants give up looking for housing
Competition for limited housing will cause landlords to lower their rental prices

title: Market for rental houses
questionText: What triggers the expansion in supply from this disequilibrium?
answers: More landlords offer rental houses to assist with the disequilibrium
Landlords see that tenants are willing to pay more an so revise down their rental prices
Fewer landlords offer rental houses to assist with the disequilibrium
Landlords see that tenants are willing to pay more an so revise up their rental prices

title: Labour Market
questionText: Consider the labour market shown. If the government were to introduce a minimum wage of $24 per hour, what disequilibrium would occur?
answers: The demand for workers is greater than the supply of workers leading to a shortage of 10,000 workers
The supply of workers is greater than the demand for workers leading to a shortage of 10,000 workers
The demand for workers is greater than the supply of workers leading to a surplus of 10,000 workers
The supply of workers is greater than the demand for workers leading to a surplus of 10,000 workers

title: market for strawberries
questionText: Consider the market for strawberries. At a price of $3.50 per kg, what triggers the price mechanism to begin?
answers: Strawberry producers have excess demand and so need to lower prices to clear their stock
Strawberry producers have excess supply and so need to lower prices to clear their stock
Strawberry producers have excess demand and so need to raise prices to clear their stock
Strawberry producers have excess supply and so need to raise prices to clear their stock

questionText: Which of the following best describes how the price mechanism leads to market clearing?
answers: government intervention in the market will ensure that there is no shortage or surplus and that the market clears
Market forces and government intervention both ensure that there is no shortage or surplus and that the market clears
Market forces of supply and demand ensure that there is no shortage or surplus and that the market clears
the price mechanism will always reduce prices to ensure that equilibrium is reached and the market clears
